_doc: Which Minecraft versions (1.21.x, then the 26.x calendar line) a fork's version branches target, and why the others are skipped.
NeoForge numbers its lines after the Minecraft minor: NeoForge 21.N builds Minecraft 1.21.N. From 26.x it carries the whole
Minecraft version instead: NeoForge 26.2.0.B builds Minecraft 26.2 and 26.1.2.B builds 26.1.2 (each Minecraft release is its
own line, so 26.1, 26.1.1 and 26.1.2 are three). 26.x needs Java 25 (the Mojang manifest's javaVersion, CATALOG V1).
A line is TARGETED only if NeoForge published a stable (non-beta) build for it: players install stable
NeoForge, and a mod built on a beta line pins a loader few people run. Measured 2026-10-12 from
per line). Re-measure with: fork-branches.py versions --refresh. The neo version below is the one the
port was measured and gated against, not necessarily the newest.
gate: 'full' runs every gate; 'compile' only compiles (a middle target between two fully gated ones).
geckolib: the GeckoLib release for that line (Modrinth, newest release for the line, measured 2026-10-12). geckolib_group:
the Maven group it is published under when not the 1.21.x one -- from 5.5 GeckoLib publishes com.geckolib:geckolib-neoforge-<mc>
on the same cloudsmith maven (software.bernie.geckolib:geckolib-neoforge-26.x is a 404, which reads as 'no 26.x build');
add-target turns it into a dependency substitution for a fork that names the old group.
nfrt: the NeoForm runtime a version branch stages with (nfrt_version), when the one ModDevGradle 2.0.146 brings (2.0.27) cannot:
it fails NeoForge 26.2.0.90's own access transformer at recompile (measured 2026-10-12; 2.0.31, MDG 2.0.148's, stages it).

lines.skip: NeoForge 21.2 never left beta (1.21.3, a hotfix of 1.21.2, followed within two weeks); a 1.21.2 player would need a beta loader
NeoForge 21.6 is beta-only (superseded by 21.8 within weeks)
